Results and ablations ::: Ablation studies	To understand the impact of some hyperparameters on performance, we conducted additional experiments on the Reuters, Polarity, and IMDB datasets, with the non-hierarchical version of MPAD.

As shown in Table TABREF29, using sum instead of mean decreases performance everywhere, suggesting that in our application, capturing the distribution of neighbor representations is more important that capturing their structure.

Except on Reuters (almost no change), performance always suffers, stressing the need to take into account the root node during updates, not only its neighborhood.
